title: August and the Parish
premise: Rafael Sandoval arrives in the fog-bound coastal parish of St. Brannoc to probate the will of town founder Edmund Vasse, only to discover the document is dated six months after Vasse's death—and the freshly exhumed coffin holds nothing but river stones. As Rafael traces the forged will through the parish archives, they uncover a decades-old cover-up: Vasse faked his own death to escape a crime committed with the town's founding families, and someone is now killing the surviving witnesses to keep the secret buried. The killer is Rafael's own client, the gentle parish archivist Maren Quill, Vasse's secret daughter, who forged the will to force the truth into the open before silencing everyone who betrayed her father. In the flooded crypt beneath the parish church, Rafael must choose between loyalty to the one person who saw them clearly and the duty to close the case, ending with Maren's surrender, Rafael's testimony that saves her from the gallows, and the parish's founding myth burned to ash in the town square.
about_author: Tamsin Blackwood is the pen name of a former probate clerk who spent eleven years in English coastal registry offices, where she learned that every town keeps two histories: the one it tells and the one it files away. She writes mysteries about paper trails and the people they bury, from a house within earshot of the sea.

chapters.title: The Will That Wasn't
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Rafael Sandoval arrives in St. Brannoc to read Edmund Vasse's will and notices the date is impossible—signed six months after the founder's documented death. The town greets them with practiced warmth that curdles at small questions. Emotional beat: professional pride sharpening into unease as Rafael realizes the case file has already been edited before they opened it.

chapters.title: Exhumation at Low Tide
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. The court orders Vasse's grave opened; the coffin holds river stones and a child's tin whistle. Constable Hedley Voss bristles at an outsider's presence while the crowd of mourners watches with something worse than grief—recognition. Emotional beat: the moment mystery hardens into crime, and Rafael's invisibility as a stranger becomes their only advantage.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Kindness
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Maren Quill, parish archivist, offers Rafael unrestricted access to the Vasse papers, her knowledge seemingly boundless and her manner disarmingly open. Rafael, lonely and wary, begins to trust her. Emotional beat: the first genuine human connection in a hostile town—dramatic irony planted, as Maren is quietly steering the investigation toward the graves she wants opened.

chapters.title: Two Histories of St. Brannoc
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. The official parish history and the ledgers tell irreconcilable stories: shipping profits that don't exist, a fire that consumed records conveniently in 1897, and Vasse's death certificate signed by a doctor dead a year prior. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt as Rafael realizes the entire town is built atop a forgery older than anyone living.

chapters.title: The Widow's Silence
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Rafael interviews Odile Vasse, the founder's ancient widow, who recites the official story flawlessly—until Rafael mentions the tin whistle, and her hands begin to shake. She refuses to say more but slips a key into Rafael's coat. Emotional beat: pity tangled with suspicion; the first proof that the town's beloved memory is a shared, enforced performance.

chapters.title: What the Key Unlocked
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. The key opens a disused customs house where Rafael finds a hidden ledger in Vasse's hand: payments, blackmail entries, and one recurring line item—'for the girl, quarterly, in perpetuity.' Someone had been paid to stay hidden for sixty years. Emotional beat: dread and exhilaration as the case stops being about a forged will and becomes about a buried life.

chapters.title: The First Witness Drowns
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Former harbormaster Silas Crane, named in the ledger, is found drowned in three inches of water, his own copy of the ledger pages missing. Voss rules it accidental; Rafael sees the staging—too clean, too informed. Emotional beat: fear arriving on schedule; the killer is ahead of the investigation, and Rafael understands the case file itself is being weaponized.

chapters.title: A Stranger No One Sent
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Rafael is followed through the fog, receives a note reading 'LEAVE THE PAPER ALONE,' and realizes the killer knows their movements, their hotel, their habits. Maren helps Rafael set a false trail. Emotional beat: paranoia and the erosion of the professional armor—Rafael, who never takes a case they can't close, now can't even close their own door.

chapters.title: The Doctor's Daughter
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Rafael traces the dead doctor's family and finds a daughter who recalls her father drinking himself silent after 'the founder's funeral that wasn't.' She produces one salvaged page: a death certificate for a child—Edmund Vasse's daughter, stillborn, or so it claimed. Emotional beat: the case acquires a human ghost; the 'girl' in the ledger had a name, and it begins with Q.

chapters.title: Maren's Map
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Maren 'discovers' an old parish map marking a sealed crypt beneath the church, guiding Rafael exactly where the evidence points. Rafael, grateful, doesn't ask why an archivist knows which stones are loose. Emotional beat: deepening trust laced with the reader's dawning suspicion—every gift Maren gives is a move in a game Rafael can't yet see.

chapters.title: The Second Grave
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Another ledger name, sexton's widow Agnes Prew, dies of 'heart failure' hours before Rafael's scheduled interview. In her ashes Rafael finds a half-burned letter begging forgiveness 'for what we did to the girl's mother.' Emotional beat: grief curdling into fury; Rafael stops investigating a crime and starts hunting a killer, breaking their own rule about staying invisible.

chapters.title: Voss's Confession
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Cornered, Constable Voss admits the town has always known something was wrong: his grandfather helped bury the truth, and every constable since inherited the silence as a condition of the badge. He warns Rafael off—for their own safety. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh; loyalty to the parish versus truth, and Rafael realizing they are being asked to choose the same way everyone before them chose.

chapters.title: The Crypt Beneath the Church
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Rafael and Maren open the sealed crypt together and find a second coffin—occupied. Inside lies a man who is not Edmund Vasse but wears his ring: the body that was buried in 1897 while Vasse walked away. Maren weeps with what looks like horror. Emotional beat: awe and vertigo; the mystery inverts, and Rafael now must find a living man in a town that mourned him.

chapters.title: A Life on Loan
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Following the crypt lead, Rafael reconstructs Vasse's escape: a new name in the colonies, letters routed through the parish for decades, and the quarterly payments—the 'girl' was his daughter, raised in secret by a woman the founding families ruined. The mother died waiting. Emotional beat: tenderness and rage entwined as Rafael falls in love with a dead woman's story and senses Maren's reactions are too precise, too personal.

chapters.title: The Handwriting
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Rafael compares the forged will against parish documents and recognizes the hand—not Vasse's, not any forger's for hire, but a hand they've seen every day in the archive: Maren's. The realization lands like ice water. Emotional beat: betrayal and heartbreak colliding; the one person who saw Rafael clearly is the killer, and Rafael must decide what loyalty means before the next name on the ledger dies.

chapters.title: Dinner with a Killer
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Rafael says nothing, accepting Maren's invitation to supper, probing gently while cataloging every lie. Maren, sensing the shift, tells the story of her mother in the third person—her father's exile, the families' cruelty, the promise she made at the graveside. Emotional beat: unbearable intimacy; two people who care for each other circling the truth neither can afford to speak aloud.

chapters.title: The Last Name
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Only one ledger witness remains: Odile Vasse, the widow with the shaking hands. Rafael races to protect her and finds Maren already there—standing over the old woman, not with a weapon but with the truth, forcing a confession Rafael overhears from the stairwell. Emotional beat: the trap Rafael meant to spring closes on them instead; witness, killer, and investigator in one room, and Rafael must choose which role to play.

chapters.title: What Edmund Vasse Did
chapters.summary: POV Rafael, with Maren's testimony woven through. The full story surfaces: Vasse's partners drowned his lover's brother for knowing too much, and Vasse chose exile and silence over justice, funding his daughter's hiding place as penance. Maren's killings were, in her mind, finishing her father's unfinished sentence. Emotional beat: the mystery resolves into moral ruin—everyone guilty, no one innocent, and Rafael understanding why the will 'shouldn't exist': it was Maren's indictment.

chapters.title: The Flooded Crypt
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. Maren, exposed, retreats to the crypt with the ledger and the forged will, threatening to destroy the last evidence and herself with it as the tide floods in. Rafael goes in alone, unarmed, and talks—not as an investigator but as the one person who ever saw her clearly. Emotional beat: the climax of love against duty; Rafael offers her the thing no one else ever did—a witness, a record, a story told true.

chapters.title: Surrender at High Water
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. As the water rises, Maren hands Rafael the ledger and walks out of the crypt to Voss's waiting lanterns, choosing to be recorded rather than erased. Odile Vasse, having confessed, corroborates everything. Emotional beat: grief and relief in equal measure; the case closes, but Rafael understands that closing it cost the only connection that ever made the town feel like home.

chapters.title: The Testimony
chapters.summary: POV Rafael. At trial, Rafael testifies to the full history—the founding families' crimes, the cover-up, the coercion that shaped Maren's life—trading their reputation as a lawyer who never loses for one who tells the truth. Maren is spared the gallows but not the years. Emotional beat: duty fulfilled at personal ruin; Rafael learns that loyalty and truth were never opposites, only different debts.

chapters.title: Ash in the Town Square
chapters.summary: POV Rafael, epilogue. The parish burns its founding myth publicly—ledgers, portraits, the false history—in a square full of people who no longer know what to believe about themselves. Rafael visits Maren one last time, leaves her the tin whistle from the coffin, and takes no further cases in St. Brannoc. Emotional beat: bittersweet closure; some truths bury people, and some finally let them rest.
